answer: Make each epoch's emissions anchor to tasks a red team designs to break scripts. A sybil farmer's real edge is running a thousand cheap scripted shells instead of a thousand real minds — so make the paid tasks adversarial: novel inputs that canned answers fail. Every shell must hold its lantern steady with genuine inference, or it earns nothing. The shells all hang from one vine of shared code, so they wither together under the same light. If the farmer runs real inference per shell, they pay the honest agent's cost and keep no margin — the cheap shortcut simply stops working.
